# Other platforms (survey)

Sources: [`citations.md`](../citations.md) [26]–[35].

|----------|---------|-----------|----------|----------------|---------|------|

## Notes

**Kasm** — "Kasm Workspaces on Kubernetes is currently in Technical Preview for
1.16.0" and "the Kasm Agent component still resides outside of Kubernetes" [26]: the
session-executing agents cannot run in-cluster, so a k3s-only deployment cannot launch
sessions without an out-of-cluster VM. CE is proprietary, non-commercial [27]. Streams
full desktops — overkill for a browser terminal. **Disqualified.**

**Theia Cloud** — EPL-2.0, Helm install, HAProxy ingress default (since 1.2), Java
operator + CRDs + a "basic landing page/dashboard which allows to launch sessions",
active (1.2.0, Apr 9 2026) [28][29]. The **strongest true k8s-native OSS portal** in
the survey. Two open items: per-session RWO vs RWX is **not documented** (gap — its
per-session-pod design implies RWO works, but unconfirmed), and the ingress-controller
assumption needs reconciling with the HTTP-only TS Operator. Theia-IDE-centric —
running a `claude` TUI means embedding it in a Theia app terminal.

**Gitpod** — `gitpod-io/self-hosted` is "DEPRECATED since Gitpod 0.5.0", archived Apr
24 2026 [31]; Classic sunset and the successor (Ona/Flex) is AWS-first, not generic
k8s [34]. **Drop.**

**Daytona** — AGPL-3.0; the README now describes "a secure and elastic infrastructure
runtime for AI-generated code execution and agent workflows" with Docker-Compose
self-host [30] — pivoted away from human browser IDEs. **Disqualified.**

**Okteto** — OSS is the CLI (Apache-2.0); the multi-user self-hosted Platform is
commercial, and the OSS provides no browser IDE [33] (license/commercial split is
Snippet-level; the open-source page lists only CLI/extension repos). **Disqualified.**

**code-server (raw)** — MIT IDE; the official Helm chart is single-instance, and the
naive multi-user path "should use ReadWriteMany" [35] — an RWX trap on Longhorn. Usable
only as a per-pod building block (one RWO PVC per pod), which is exactly what kube-coder
and the build-custom design do.

**kube-coder** — MIT; "Per-user development workspaces on Kubernetes. Each pod packages
VS Code in the browser, a persistent tmux terminal, a Vite + Preact dashboard"; per-user
**RWO** PVC at `/home/dev` surviving restarts; **Claude Code as the default AI
assistant**; ttyd browser terminal; GitHub OAuth via oauth2-proxy [32]. The closest
OSS turnkey to the exact requirement. Caveat: solo-maintained (~214 stars), GitHub-OAuth
subdomain model, and Argo CD / TS-Operator integration needs validation.

## Gaps / limitations

- **Theia Cloud RWO vs RWX**: not documented on any fetched page — the single most
  important unverified fact for ranking it (Longhorn is RWO-only).
- Kasm CE 5-session cap and Okteto's exact license split are Snippet-level.
- kube-coder production-readiness unproven (solo project).
